answer: Each identity adopts one named veteran tree from the ancient-tree register: one oak rooted on a limestone ledge, recorded once, never twice. Yearly the steward measures its girth and taps the trunk — a sound trunk answers with a dull echo — then files the survey by lantern light, county-countersigned. One tree backs one identity; duplicates refused. Each fake costs one real tree, 900 units, 120 days; 100 fakes: 90,000 units, 100 trees, 12,000 days. Cheapest cheat: hire a surveyor to file for another name — they spend the one tree they could claim, and a forged girth fails the re-measure.
